summary: Ethernet controller firmware reset rewrites NIC serial, blocking Intune/Autopilot provisioning after depot repair
description:
Issue summary:
After depot repair and vendor-supplied firmware refresh of the Intel Ethernet controller, affected machines receive a different NIC hardware serial (HWID) reported by the OS. This change prevents the device from matching its existing Intune/Autopilot record, blocking policy application and certificate provisioning. Impact is seen for devices returning from depot repair/planned firmware refresh where the vendor's flasher rewrites controller identifiers.

Impact:
- Devices fail Intune device sync and remain in "staged" state in Autopilot, preventing user sign-in flows.
- VPN/certificate provisioning (machine cert enrollment via SCEP) times out because the device identity does not match inventory.
- Affects recent depot repairs for two laptop lines in us-west and a small number in us-east; blocking 12 active provisioning flows so far.

Environment:
- Corp provisioning lab (us-west) and limited production returns (us-east).
- Windows 11 Enterprise 22H2 image built with corporate depot image builder v4.3.
- Intune + Autopilot enrollment, SCEP-based machine certs via internal CA.

Expected behavior:
- NIC firmware refresh should not alter the HWID/serial presented to OS or MDM. Devices should re-attach to existing Intune records after imaging or firmware updates.

Actual behavior:
- OS reports a different Physical Address ID/HWID for the Ethernet controller. Intune's device matching logic treats device as unsupported/new, leaving it in pending enrollment state.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send affected unit to depot repair with request for NIC firmware update.
2) Depot applies vendor firmware tool (Intel/Realtek flasher) and returns device.
3) Re-image machine with corporate image (or boot normally).
4) Observe device in Intune; device record does not match expected inventory HWID.
5) Attempt Autopilot/Intune sync and SCEP machine cert enrollment — it fails with mismatch/timeouts.
logs:
Sample event snippets:
- Device manager: Ethernet Controller (Intel X710) - HWID: 0xAB12CD34 => after firmware: 0x1F34BE77
- Intune enrollment log: 2026-03-09T15:22:08Z ERROR DeviceMatchFailed: hwid mismatch (expected=AB12CD34, observed=1F34BE77)
- SCEP proxy log: 2026-03-09T15:22:12Z ERROR CertificateRequest: device not in inventory (serial mismatch)
- Syslog (provisioning node): 2026-03-09T15:22:13Z WARN AutopilotState: pending (device_id=null)
investigation_notes: Confirmed pattern across 8 depot-returned units: all underwent vendor NIC firmware refresh before return.
Compared pre-repair asset DB snapshot to post-repair: HWID changed in OS-level enumeration (pnputil/ipconfig /all shows new identifier).
Checked imaging process: corporate image does not run any NIC re-provisioning logic that would rewrite HWIDs.
Spoke with depot vendor: their flasher has an option to reset controller persistent ID; this was enabled in recent firmware package.
Verified Intune matching logic: primary matching uses SMBIOS serial + NIC HWID as a secondary key for devices without full Autopilot pre-registration; mismatch blocks SCEP machine cert issuance.
Reproduced locally using vendor flasher in lab: toggling 'reset persistent ID' yields the observed change.
Risk assessment: Broad roll of vendor firmware with reset flag could affect all devices of this NIC family; remediation required before sending more units to depot for that firmware.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:14 - Anya Patel: Customer-facing impact is internal users returning from depot are unable to sign in. Opening ticket after SRE confirmed reproducible change.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Marco Reyes: Assigned to me for triage. Replicated with 2 units in lab; seems vendor flasher toggles a 'reset id' bit by default in v1.2.4.
2026-03-12 13:30 - Depot Support (via #depot-support): Vendor acknowledged the option and provided a temp build without the reset toggle. Requesting how many units were affected.
2026-03-13 09:45 - IT Ops: Blocked new depot submissions for Dell-Precision-5480 until we confirm flasher settings; created intake hold.

2026-03-14 08:20 - Marco Reyes: Workaround validated: vendor-provided flasher (no-reset build) restores original HWID when applied; manual reflash required for returned units. Preparing SOP and pre-check script.
2026-03-14 12:05 - Anya Patel: Noted that 4 business-critical returns were unblocked using manual reflash + Intune re-sync. Need permanent fix in depot SOP.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Vendor-provided non-reset firmware flasher applied to affected units to restore original HWID, then Intune device sync retriggered resulting in successful Autopilot/device state reconciliation.
Short-term mitigation: Hold placed on depot firmware package v1.2.4 that includes reset flag. Depot instructed to use supplied no-reset build for affected SKUs.

Medium-term fix: Imaging pipeline will include a pre-provision HWID verification script that compares OS NIC HWID to asset DB and flags mismatches before Intune enrollment. Script PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-tools/pull/482.

Follow-ups: 1) Update Depot SOP to validate flasher settings and disable persistent-ID reset. 2) Expand intake checklist to include 'NIC persistent ID' validation for returns. 3) Add an alert in provisioning console when more than 1% of returns show HWID mismatches.
Owners: Marco Reyes (SRE) to deliver provisioning pre-check; Depot Manager (Lina Morales) to enforce vendor flasher settings. Target: complete mitigations by 2026-03-21.
Status: Partial resolution — immediate reworks done for impacted units, process changes in progress.
